paper_metadata.title: Improving the Sequence Alignment Method by Quantum Multi-Pattern Recognition

summary: The paper proposes a Grover-like quantum multi-pattern recognition method applied to dot-matrix sequence alignment, requiring approximately T ≈ (π/4)√(N/n) iterations and achieving theoretical 100% recognition probability when the learning pattern set exceeds one-third of all patterns. In the example, sequences are split into 50‑digit fragments (≈32 runs) with a conceptual search space of 2^50 ≈ 1.13×10^15 patterns, compared against classical dynamic programming estimated at >7.2×10^6 operations. No hardware implementation or simulation results are provided.

experiments.description: Hybrid sequence-alignment experiment using a dot-matrix formulation combined with a quantum multi-pattern recognition method based on Grover-like search to identify matching diagonal regions in pairwise sequence alignment.

algorithm.variant: quantum multi-pattern recognition / improved Grover-like search

hyperparameters.success_probability: 100% when learning pattern set exceeds 1/3 of total patterns
hyperparameters.pattern_set_fraction: n and s close to 1/3 of total patterns

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state |φ0⟩ prepared by encoding the learning pattern set into a superposition

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary patterns and spurious states are encoded as basis states in a superposition; each full diagonal of the dot matrix is treated as a one-dimensional binary dataset of equal length to the target patterns
problem_formulation.objective_function: Identify matching diagonal regions in a dot-matrix sequence alignment by recognizing pattern states with high probability
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Pattern set and spurious set sizes satisfy s = n and s + n < 2^i; example uses fragmentation of long sequence into smaller pieces

problem_instance.description: Pairwise sequence alignment on dot-matrix plots for biological sequences; example uses XL23808 and XLRHODOP DNA sequences
problem_instance.dataset_name: EMBL DNA sequences XL23808 and XLRHODOP

dataset_specification.description: Dot plot example from European Molecular Biology Laboratory; vertical sequence divided into 50-digit pieces; 1600/50 ≈ 32 applications

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Dot-matrix recurrence plot construction; full diagonals extracted as datasets; shorter diagonals padded to equal length
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Illustrative example application; no formal benchmark protocol reported

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical dot-matrix post-processing / classical assembly of fragments
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct dot-matrix recurrence plot; split long sequence into smaller fragments; encode diagonals as binary datasets
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical methods assemble the puzzle with the diagonals in the plot; local SA applied after quantum spotting

speedup_claims.conditions: for the Grover-like multi-pattern recognition search; example uses fragments of 50 digits and pattern set size close to 1/3 of total patterns
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper gives asymptotic iteration count and claims polynomial-time spotting of similar regions, but no hardware implementation or wall-clock timing is reported.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: quantum multi-pattern recognition with learning pattern set exceeding 1/3 of total patterns
speedup_claims.conditions: when the learning pattern set exceeds 1/3 of the overall patterns
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a stated property of the adopted algorithm, not an experimentally measured probability on hardware.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(√(N/n)) iterations for the Grover-like search; described as polynomial time in the conclusion
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(s1·s2) for classical dynamic programming methods
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: Approximately 32 runs in the example (one per 50-digit fragment)
complexity_analysis.total_operations_classical: More than 7.2×10^6 computing steps in the example

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require encoding very large dot‑matrix diagonal datasets (example uses fragments of length 50 implying a search space of 2^50 ≈ 1.13×10^15 states) and implementing Grover‑like iterations with sufficient qubits to represent pattern indices and datasets; the paper provides no concrete circuit or qubit estimates.
limiting_factors: No explicit circuit construction or qubit count provided
State preparation for large pattern sets would be extremely costly
No empirical benchmarks or runtime measurements
Hybrid pipeline still relies on classical alignment post-processing

notes: No hardware or circuit implementation details are reported; hardware and qubit count are not specified in the paper.
